answer: Each seat must own a registered low-power radio band, capped at one per legal entity. Every epoch it sends its nonce as a short whisper in cipher over that band, and three independent monitoring stations must hear it. Two seats on one band garble each other, so clones cannot pool a license: a k-seat farm needs k registered bands, and scarcity pricing plus duplicate cuts keep that cost rising faster than headcount. A seat whose signal drops to its nadir for a full round forfeits the band.
